newsitem.title: FRANCE: French rail drivers' union calls strike.
newsitem.headline: French rail drivers' union calls strike.

text.p: A leading trade union in France's state-owned SNCF railways called on Tuesday for a nationwide strike later this month to protest against a restructuring plan.
The train drivers' branch of the pro-Socialist CFDT, France's biggest union, urged its members to launch a stoppage as soon as the Senate starts debating the plan on January 21.
"This proposal will be put forward to other unions at a meeting on January 15," the CFDT said in a statement.
The centre-right government plans to split the loss-making SNCF in two with one group in charge of infrastructure and inheriting debts associated with it.

Most trade unions have backed the reform but the CFDT and the Communist-led CGT, which claims a majority in the SNCF, have opposed it. French rail traffic came to a virtual standstill for three weeks during nationwide protests by train drivers in late 1995.
